definitions.explanation: The number 5,000, formed as {五|ご} (five) × {千|せん} (1,000). No sound change occurs.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{五千|ごせん}{歩|ほ}しか{歩|ある}かなかった。
examples.english: I only walked five thousand steps today.

examples.japanese: その{寺|てら}は{五千|ごせん}{年|ねん}とは{言|い}わないが、{千年|せんねん}{以上|いじょう}の{歴史|れきし}があるそうだ。
examples.english: The temple isn't five thousand years old, but it apparently has over a thousand years of history.

notes:
Formed as {五|ご} × {千|せん}. Among the thousands, only three combinations change sound — worth memorizing as a set.

SOUND CHANGES IN THE THOUSANDS:
- {三千|さんぜん}: 3,000 — せん voices to ぜん
- {八千|はっせん}: 8,000 — はち shortens to はっ
- {一千|いっせん}: 1,000 — いち shortens to いっ
- {五千|ごせん}, {四千|よんせん}, {六千|ろくせん}, {七千|ななせん}, {九千|きゅうせん}: regular

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {五千|ごせん}{円|えん}{札|さつ}: five-thousand-yen note, which bears the portrait of {樋口|ひぐち}{一葉|いちよう}
- {五千|ごせん}{人|にん}: five thousand people
- {五千|ごせん}{歩|ほ}: five thousand steps
